content:
Elaine: Quick Q — I'm migrating the payments svc to use ExternalSecrets pointing at Vault KV v2. Changing tf module to generate ExternalSecret with annotations for refresh/lease. Concern: the app mounts the secret as a projected volume (projected token from Vault Agent sidecar). If the projected token TTL is short (<60s) I've seen app crash loops because the file didn't update. Anyone seen this? Should we 1) bump projection TTL, 2) rely on CSI secrets-store, or 3) switch to Secret->env so kube updates are synced? PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/trees/feat/vault-extsecret

Ryan: We hit this last quarter. Short answer: projected volumes are 'write-once' by kubelet; updates to the Secret don't atomically remount files unless using CSI. So if you depend on in-place file updates you need a reloader or use secrets-store CSI driver with provider-vault.

Priya: Another wrinkle: Vault Agent sidecar can renew token, but the app's file handle may not detect changes. Our pattern was to let ExternalSecrets sync into a Kubernetes Secret and mount as env or use a lightweight sidecar that tails the file and signals the process.

Priya: Example TF snippet we added to the platform module:

module "payments_extsecret" {
  source = "git::ssh://git.internal/infra/modules/external-secret.git//k8s?ref=v2.1"

  name        = "payments-vault"
  namespace   = "payments"
  vault_path  = "secret/data/services/payments"
  annotations = {
    "external-secrets.io/refresh" = "45s"
    "external-secrets.io/reconcile-timeout" = "20s"
  }
}

Ryan: On the k8s manifest side we used ExternalSecret + secret -> mount env. Example:

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1beta1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: payments-creds
  annotations:
    external-secrets.io/refresh: "45s"
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    name: vault-store
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
  target:
    name: payments-creds
    creationPolicy: Owner
  data:
  - secretKey: api_key
    remoteRef:
      key: secret/data/services/payments
      property: api_key

Ryan: If you must keep projected volumes, then the CSI secrets-store is the only reliable way to ensure file content updates without restarting pods. Otherwise switch to env or plan a sidecar that sends SIGHUP to process.

deploy-bot: plan applied to staging (terraform/infra: ref feat/vault-extsecret). No risky changes in prod yet. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: Note — rotation job will create new versions in Vault; make sure ExternalSecrets has `watch` annotations. Also, if you set TTL < 60s you may need to raise the token renew window in vault-agent config.

Elaine: Awesome, thanks. I'll update the module to default to 45s refresh and add docs suggesting CSI for projected volume use-cases. Opening PR now, will ping for review. @ryan @priya :sparkles:

Ryan: LGTM, small nit: add a test that mounts as env and as projected volume in staging to validate restart behavior.

Priya: I'll review the PR and add a how-to in docs/ops/secrets.md about reloader vs CSI.

Elaine: cheers, closing loop — will add upgrade note for on-prem customers about CSI driver requirement.
